title: Squint in the sun
story:
“Get up for the trip!” sings mum. “It’s cold! Tuck me in my quilt
and I can be snug.” “Come on,” mum calls. “Get up!”
At long last the van is set up and we can rest. “Quack, quack.”
“What was that?”
“Quick, mum! A flock of ducks have come to visit us.”
Mum squints in the sun to see the ducks. My pals are quick and
swift and sprint past the bins.
Dump and run to the next thing. Where are my pals?
I am off on a quest to get them.
All my pals are on the sand! We squint in the sun. I am quick and
sprint with a bat in hand.
Next, I am in for a swim! I squish and squelch in the wet sand.
It will melt if you are not quick.
Lick, lick as the sun sets on all the fun.

title: Mitch and the itch
story:
Mitch lives to jump and give an itch.
A pinch on the chin, legs and back. Mitch will catch us in a damp
ditch or on the land.
Mitch is quick to jump on this chest. Pinch, pinch, such a pest to
delve in and nest.
Twitch, twitch. That must have been Mitch!
Is this a soft patch for Mitch to lay some eggs?
“A soft bed for me to rest,” Mitch thinks.
“Rich and plush for a big batch of us.”
Get up, Cali! Fetch a stick. Run! Here comes Mitch! Cali is still and
Mitch is quick.
A soft patch for Mitch to lay some eggs! The eggs hatch.
Cali will scratch and scratch.

title: A trek up the track
story:
Mum and Nana send us on a trek up the track where
we can dig for ants.
Mum stops, “Can you spot the black ants, with strips of gold on
their backs?”
Mum clamps her hands on the long stick. “The ants are small, but
we must be strong when we dig.”
Mum has a rest on the crest of the pit.
Cram and sit in the pit. Flick and sift the sand with the long stick.
A clump of sand in the cup of her hands. Mum has the skill to get
the ants with the black and gold strips.
A quick pinch on their back. The trick is not to get a nip from the
ants.
“Thank you, mum!” I hold the ant and suck on my snack. Yum!

title: Max with Mum’s list
story:
Max is a whiz at the shops with Mum’s list.
With a scratch and a twitch, it is a stretch to think of all the things
on the list. “A tin of fish, a whisk…what next?” Max must check
Mum’s list.
Max picks up a tin of fish and a whisk. Tick it off the list!
Max whacks some chips in on a whim. “I’d best grab a bag of rolls
from the list.” Tick!
Mum has twelve carrots on the list. Max twists their tops to get
them to fit.
“I think Mum will whip up some eggs and milk with the whisk.”
There is a tick for all the things on Mum’s list. Max did well.
Mum gives Max a big hug when he is back from the shops.
“Thanks, Max.”

title: Sant and Kale
story:
Sant the ant and his pal Kale the snail, play on the trail. It is a hot day.
Sant tricks Kale and hops in a tin. Will he wait long?
Sant plays next to the tap. It is a great game to stomp in the thick mud.
The pals take the train across the trail. The train is quick and the wind
whips up.
On the way, Sant spots his mate, Buzz. They stop to have a game of chase.
They are so glad for the fish and chip shop! Sant and Kale stay and
take a break for lunch.
At last, Sant and Kale sit on a rock. They have lunch in the shade.
What fun they had today!
It is getting late, so Sant and Kale sit to rest. It is a great sunset.
They make plans to play the next day.

title: Three great mates
story:
Sant made plans to meet his mate Spotty at the creek. He is happy, thinking
of all the fun games to play that sunny day.
Just then, Spotty popped out from a great big tree. Sant is happy to see his
mate, Spotty.
Spotty jumps in the creek. The creek is too deep for Sant the ant. Will Sant
reach Spotty? Sant can see some bark. It can carry Sant to Spotty.
Sant sings when he is happy. “My pal, Buzz-Bee, eats sweet treats.
Oh, so yummy in his tummy!” Spotty sways along to the song with glee.
“Did you say Buzz-Bee? That’s me!” It is Sant’s mate, Buzz.
“Great to see you Buzz! Please meet my mate, Spotty,” says Sant.
The team of three are messy from their fun at the creek. They need to brush
off the mud to get clean.
Buzz, Sant and Spotty eat sweet treats next to the creek.
Spotty, Buzz and Sant are three great mates. They agree to meet next week
by the great big tree.

title: Sant the disco ant
story:
Sant is happy when he sings. His dream is to sing at the disco with his
bandmates up the road. Sant phones to ask if he can visit. They say, “Yes!”
He only needs to take a quick stroll up the road to meet his bandmates.
The song notes from the band float to Sant as he goes up the road.
Clint and Ash know that to be the best and grow, they must play the same
beat over and over.
Ned can play along when the beat is known. His bass is low. He follows the
beat well and taps his toes.
Jaz taps her tapping sticks. The song is growing and there is no way
of knowing when Sant will sing. He is waiting for his big break.
Here comes Sant, he is singing with the band. He opens his arms
and puffs out his chest. Singing is what he knows best!
The tempo is slow. Sant asks to speed up the tempo so they can play
the song at the disco.
Sant’s dream to sing at the disco is real. He is so happy to know that
he is part of the disco.

title: Sant’s first race
story:
It is Sant’s first race day! He has a yellow shirt to show the team he is
running for.
Shan is running for the purple team. Her sister looks on from the stand.
The runners burst onto the track. Their feet beat the dirt of the track,
as they turn into the first bend.
The dirt kicks up and their team mates cheer. Jack and Tim run fast,
as the track turns. Tim jerks close to Jack. He works hard to be first.
Their mates clap and twirl from the stand. They can’t wait to see
who will be first. Even the birds chirp and watch from the stand!
The runners can see the finish flag. Their legs hurt, but they keep
running as fast as they can. Sant is puffing and sprinting now.
Shan is close to Sant.
Sant wins the race! It is the yellow team’s turn to take the winning cup.
Sant feels on top of the world.
Fern is Shan’s sister. She is the first to say how well she ran.
Fern was clapping for her every lap of the race

title: Quest to the shed
story:
Nick and Tina grab hats for their heads and set off to see their mate, Rick.
“Rick may be resting by his tree again,” says Tina.
Rick isn’t resting when they see him. He is ready to jump and play.
Nick and Tina have taken a bag of hats. “Is there a hat that fits you Rick?”
asks Tina. “I am not meant to have a hat, but they are fun. I will have the
black and red hat,” says Rick.
When Rick pops on his red and black hat he feels ready to go on a quest.
“Where can we go on a quest?” asks Rick.
Nick and Tina chose funny hats as well. “There is an old chest kept in
the shed,” says Tina. “Can we make this our quest?” “Yes!” they all say.
Some bits of sticky bread and jam lead to the shed.
Who has dropped these bits of bread and jam?
“What could dwell in this shed?” asks Tina. “Are we meant to be here?”
asks Rick. “It’s okay, this is our sport shed,” said Nick.
They see the chest. “Let’s open the lid,” Tina says.
Sant jumps from the chest! He has been eating bread with jam spread.
It has been a great quest!

title: Lilly’s loud crowd
story:
Lilly steps out onto the baseball pitch. There is a murmur from the crowd
as she reaches the plate.
Sant, Spotty and Buzz have come into town to see Lilly’s team play.
The crowd is loud as they begin to cheer. Lilly swings and misses her first ball.
The pitcher frowns as she waits for the catcher to be ready. There is no sound
as the crowd holds their breath.
The ball comes again. Lilly swings at it. Whack! The ball bounds over the
players and the crowd stands up to see who will catch it.
It is Mayer who stops the ball. Lilly pounds the dirt as she runs.
She counts as she moves around to each plate.
“Throw it!” A mixed sound comes from the crowd. Some shout and some are
as silly as clowns, happily cheering their team.
Lilly slides to the ground as “Safe!” is yelled. She is not out and lucky to reach
home base.
Lilly’s friends crowd around and lift her up. They are so proud of the way she
ran and didn’t give up.

title: Cooper and Tan-Tan
story:
Cooper’s best friend is his dog, TanTan. He is there when Cooper feels
happy or blue. Everyday Tan-Tan and Cooper have fun together.
“Can I get a dog chew for Tan-Tan at the shop Mum?” asks Cooper.
“Yes,” says his Mum, “you can grab me some glue and a new broom too.”
Tan-Tan and Cooper are at the shop. “You can wait here, dogs are
not allowed in. I will be back soon.” Cooper pats Tan-Tan.
At the check-out, Cooper sees Sant the ant’s dad. “I will take this broom,
some glue and a dog chew, please.” “Here you are, Cooper,” Sant’s dad
grins.
Cooper can see Tan-Tan is waiting where he left him. “You wait so well,
Tan-Tan. Here comes Spotty, Sant and Buzz. Hi crew!” says Cooper.
“Hello, Cooper and Tan-Tan,” shout the crew of friends.
“That’s a great balloon!” says Cooper. “Thanks. It’s for Nana.
We are heading to her house to see what flowers bloom in June.
Do you want to come too?” asks Sant. “Yes, please,” says Cooper.
Nana lives next to the sand dunes. “If we stand on top of the dunes,
we can just see the flowers that are in bloom,” says Spotty.
“Hello Nana, we have come to see your flowers in bloom,” Cooper says.
“These are Sturt Desert Peas. You can take some home.” Nana waves.
“Thank you, Nana!” Cooper and his friends head home.

title: Ride a bike or fly a kite
story:
Nick has a bright smile on his face. He is thinking of all the things he likes to
do. What will he fly? Where will he ride?
Nick’s friend Tammy is out for a ride on her blue bike. How many friends can
she find? The sun is high in the sky and it is a great day for a ride.
Tammy is lucky to find her friends. Nick and Ivy run to catch up with her.
They feel wild and free as they fly down the street.
“It’s my turn to ride my bike.” Nick rides at the speed of light! Sant spots Nick
as he zooms down the street on his bright, red bike.
“I like the way you fly down the street on your bike, Nick. Can I fly on your kite,
high in the sky?” Sant asks. “Yes, Sant! You can take a ride on my kite.”
Nick smiles.
Sant and the Kite fly into the tree! “I will get you down, Sant”. Nick reaches
up to Sant. “I don’t mind hanging out in this tree for a while,” Sant says with
a smile.
“You can have a turn on my bike, Ivy,” Tammy offers. “I don’t know if I can,”
sighs Ivy. “You can do it if you try. I will run along by your side,” smiles Tammy.
“Thanks, Tammy. You are very kind,” says Ivy.
Nick and Sant see Ivy on Tammy’s bike. “You can do it, Ivy!” Nick and Sant
call. “That’s right, hang on tight and keep your eye on where you want to go.”
“I can ride a bike!” Ivy squeals with pride.

title: Camping in the bush
story:
Pam is camping in the bush with her family. The tent is up and now it’s time
to have some fun. “Would you like to play a game of hide and seek?”
Pam asks her brother Zak.
“Yes Pam, I will count with my buddy Sant,” Zak yells. “Ready or not, here we
come! Now, where could she be? There are lots of spots to hide in the bush,
Pam could be anywhere!”
“I found you! That was too quick.” Zak chuckles. “Let’s go and find Tig.
I think he is napping down by the brook,” Pam says.
Tig has put himself by the fire for a cozy nap. “Should we wake him?
He looks so happy, we shouldn’t wake him,” Zak says quietly.
“What shall we cook for dinner?” asks Dad. “Fill the pot with all sorts
of veggies and a chook,” says Pam. “Yum, it smells good!” says Dad.
The tent shook in the wind that night. Sant and the siblings couldn’t hear it,
they were giggling.
“Can you hear a ‘chirp’ and a ‘woof’? Tig must be barking at the birds again,”
Pam says. “Would you be quiet Tig!” yells Zak.
They read a good book and have a full tummy of food.
Now they are all quietly sleeping.

title: A day with Doug
story:
Sant is visiting his cousin Doug. “It’s been a long time, Sant, have you been
keeping out of trouble?” smiles Doug. “I think so, Doug. Can you show me
around your town?” asks Sant.
“Here come brothers, Jon and Lea, they love to drive. Quick, jump up on their
car, Sant. You never know where they are heading next. They are double trou-
ble, like us,” Doug giggles.
Jon and Lea drop the cousins off at the trucks. Doug helps to drive the forklift.
He jumps up on the seat and lifts the heavy crates high above the ground.
The crates can weigh a ton.
Sant is in luck and jumps up on the crate for a nap. He dreams of a yummy
honey treat. “It’s no time for sleeping, Sant. Wake up or I will come up and give
you a shove!” yells Doug. Sant wakes with a jump!
“I want to show you the school,” says Doug. “This is Mr Young, he is one of the
teachers. Mr Young was in the School Fun Run and he won!”
“The kids love it when Mr Young takes them outside to run and jump. They are
lucky to have a teacher who is lots of fun,” Says Doug.
“Look Sant, here is Ann and Nat playing chase. Ann is chasing Nat. Ann can
touch Nat’s arm and then she sits down. Nat is stuck and counts to ten, then
she can run again,” explains Doug.
At the end of their big day, they see Nana. “Hello Doug and Sant! Come and
sit by the fire. Have you been looking after each other?” asks Nana. “Yes, Nana.
Doug has shown me all over the town!” Sant beams.

title: Spotty’s birthday
story:
It is the day of Spotty’s birthday party! Spotty is excited, waiting for his friends to
come to his house and celebrate.
Buzz, Sant and Doug arrive. Spotty has lots of games planned. “Hello, it’s good to
see you all,” Spotty beams. “Put on a fancy party hat and get ready for the fun!”
The pals rush onto the grass to start bowling. Sant is ready. He runs, jumps and
with a quick bounce, he rolls the ball. STRIKE! All the pins are down.
“Listen,” Buzz whispers, “Spotty’s mum is calling us back for snacks.”
They run back to find Spotty’s mum with sweet honey treats laid out.
“What else is there to play Spotty?” asks Doug. “Pass the parcel is the next game”,
Spotty says. Inside each layer is a toy mouse. Sant lets out a playful squeal.
“Dance and Freeze is a fun party game,” says Doug as he starts to bounce.
“Yes!” Spotty jumps up. “Let’s dance. Listen and try to stop when the song stops.”
Everyone lines up and gets ready to play pin the tail on Spotty. “Press the tail onto
the poster. Try not to miss,” Spotty explains. Buzz steps up. This is her chance to try
and she is spot on!
It’s time to go and Spotty’s mum is happy to pass the party bags around to the
pals. “Thanks for coming,” smiles Spotty. “Thanks, Spotty. It was a great party,”
Spotty’s friends chime.

title: Little legs on the hill
story:
Ned the numbat huffs and puffs up the big hill. Will his little legs carry him all the
way to the top? Sant the ant sits on Ned’s back. It is a good way to travel up the
hill.
At the top, Ned sits to have a rest. They can see a long way from the top of the hill.
Sant has a towel to wipe Ned’s brow. Ned looks back to see if his mate Wilbur the
wombat is following him.
Wilbur plods up the big hill. He hopes to catch up to Ned and Sant soon.
Wilbur’s little legs move at double speed to reach the top.
Ned and Sant are glad to finally see Wilbur scramble to the top of the hill.
Wilbur smiles to his friends as he looks out to the vast landscape. It is rocky with
lots of rubble beneath their feet.
Uncle Len struggles up the hill. He can remember a time when he was young and
limber. Gone are the days he could quickly bound up the hill.
Ned, Wilbur, Sant and Uncle Len are glad to reach the top of the hill. From a
distance they can hear giggles and little feet moving quickly up the big hill and
over the rubble.
Twins, Wanita and Zack bound to the top of the hill with a big smile. If there was
a medal for running fast, they would be the winners. They follow Uncle Len to the
top.
Everyone agrees, the prize to reach the top of the big hill is to look out across the
land. The air smells fresh. The leaves on the trees gently rustle in the breeze.
This will be a place to visit again.

title: A warm autumn day
story:
It is a warm autumn day at the water hole. The water is still and everything is quiet.
This morning, Spotty is laying in the sun on a warm rock. He can hear the distant,
playful call of boys heading his way.
Wilfred, Gavin and Brad decide to walk to the water hole to cool off. Brad finds a
rope hanging from a tree. He will use it to fly into the middle. Gavin jumps in.
“Look out, here I come!” he warns.
Brad hauls on the rope and swings across the water. He holds on and looks down
for a good place to fall. He stalls, but there is no going back. He has to let go!
Brad falls with a great big SPLASH! He can feel the cool water and starts to relax.
The splash causes the water to ripple and move a log closer to the middle of the
water hole.
Spotty sees Brad’s brave entry into the water hole. He jumps in and calls out to
Brad, “This log would make a good boat!” They clamber onto the floating log and
Spotty sprawls back, catching the warm autumn sun.
I think I could have a go at balancing on the log,” Gavin calls. “Steady as you go.
Make small movements to get on, or you may cause the log to roll,”
Spotty explains. The boys giggle and try sitting tall to keep good balance.
Wilfred begins to taunt his friends. “I don’t think you can stay on the log. It’s going
to roll!” Brad and Gavin feel the log roll to one side and know that they will fall.
SPLASH! “Let’s play water wars,” announces Gavin. They begin to splash each
other.
Wilfred uses the log to flip from, while Brad and Gavin hold it steady. Spotty can
feel a yawn coming on. He is ready for another nap in the warm sun. The boys talk
about how wonderful it is to play at the water hole. Maybe next time they can
make a fort close by and stay all day.

title: Hands in the air
story:
Zack and Kev meet to shoot some hoops at the local school. It is fair to say they
both have a natural flair for the game.
Kev is quick and his feet dance across the goal circle. Zack wants the ball and
glares at Kev. Where will Zack dart next? Kev’s stare has put Zack off his game.
Kev steals the ball from Zack. He dribbles it away and jumps high into the air.
Can he reach all the way up there? The wind whips his hair as he leaps.
Kev lands calling, “Yes!” The goal feels great.
Zack chases the ball down, turns, squares up to the ring and shoots. He stops and
bounces the ball twice. He takes in a deep breath to push the ball up and in the
hoop. Zack and Kev stare as the ball drops in.
Zack and Kev make a great pair. They play on the same team and love to play
offence. They are working on being fair and taking turns to share the ball.
“Where is that beat coming from?” Zack questions. “I can hear it too. It’s coming
from over there,” says Kev. “I swear that sounds like Dan.” “Do we dare follow the
melody to find out?” asks Zack.
“Hi friends, my name is Dan. I am the king of hip hop! Can you hear the melody
blare from my speakers? By my bright green van you can hear my hip hop flair,”
Dan sings in the street.
“One show only, with my mates Buzz, Sant and Spotty,” Dan raps. “We want to
show that we care. It is our hope that you treat each other fair. To share is to show
that you care. Everybody, put your hands in the air!”

title: Let’s unite!
story:
Jennifer and Cooper were unimpressed at recess time. Their class mates had made
a huge mess and rubbish was strewn across the playground. They knew that
something had to change.
“What are we going to do? It is sad to see our playground in such a mess.
Don’t they value our tidy school?” says an upset Cooper. “This isn’t worth a feud.
We must find a way to unite and keep our playground tidy,” says Jennifer.
“Did you say, unite?” Sant has come to help. “Hi, Sant. You are right on cue.
We can’t use our playground with all this strewn rubbish.”
“I am happy to help, but I feel sad that people refuse to use the bin,” Sant shares
his feelings. “Let’s use tongs to pick up the rubbish,” says Jennifer. “We are few.
We need many hands to help,” added Cooper. “Let’s spread the news to help clean
up.”
Jennifer and Cooper make posters to spread the news about putting litter in the
bin. “If we unite and work together, our school grounds will be as good as new.
The recess bell is due to ring soon. Who is with us?” Jennifer calls.
“It is good to hear no one argue,” Sant notes. “Everyone seems happy to help.”
“It feels good to unite for a common cause. Thanks for chipping in. You are all a
huge help,” Jennifer smiles.
It is a great outcome. “All those who helped now value our tidy school,” Cooper
says happily, “I knew you could do it!” Sant beams. “Look what you can do when
you spread the news and unite as a team.”
Jennifer and Cooper decide it is time to play. Sant is right. Their playground is now
as good as new. It is a huge difference to walk through their tidy school.

title: Avoid sharp rocks
story:
Tom drives a truck for work and enjoys the company of his dog, Harry, sitting
beside him. They deliver farm goods to loyal customers. Today they are dropping
off a bale of hay to farmer Roy.
Tom drives over a sharp rock in the road. It makes a big noise. “Oh no, not a flat
tyre!” Tom groans. “Well boy, we will have to deploy the spare tyre.”
“We don’t have much choice. We will have to fix this. Our first step is to make the
truck safe and pull on the handbrake. Join me outside the truck, Harry.” Tom finds
the spare wheel and tools.
“We need to loosen the wheel, jack up the truck, hoist the tyre off and place it on
the ground. Next, we need to slide the spare wheel onto the hub bolts and tighten
the nuts.” Just as well Harry likes to listen to Tom’s voice.
Tom is about to lower the truck when he notices something moist. “Hang on a tick.
The ground is moist under here.” Tom is worried. “This isn’t good. We have a loose
coil and an oil leak,“ says Tom.
Doug is out driving his new tow truck with his cousin Sant. He sees Tom on the side
of the road in turmoil and stops to help. “Boy, am I glad to see you! We are not
having much joy today,” Tom calls to Sant and Doug.
“An oil leak and a flat tyre! We will tow your truck away for repairs,” says Doug.
“I wish I was able to avoid that sharp rock,” Tom replies. “I can see your point.
How annoying!” Doug exclaims.
Farmer Roy is out driving his ute. “I’m sorry to spoil your day,” Tom calls to Roy.
“My truck has been towed away. I can’t deliver your hay.” “Bad luck about your
truck Tom. I’m just glad you’re okay. I would still employ you any day.”

title: Sant’s blast off
story:
The Year 4 teacher, Mr Arthur, is keen to share a science experiment with his class.
The boys have been asking for a while to make rockets. “I can’t wait to see how far
it can blast into the sky,” Paul says.
“There are a few steps to follow. First, fill your bottle past the halfway mark.
Next, place a fizzy tablet into the bottle and make sure the lid is on tight. Please
ask if you get stuck.” Mr Arthur enjoys explaining science tasks.
“Hi, class! I hear you are making rockets. Can I hop on one of your bottle rockets
and visit the stars?” Sant asks. “Yes, Sant! You need to keep calm when the rocket
takes off,” says Paul.
The final step is to turn the bottle upside down in the jar. “Are you ready to be the
first ant in space, Sant?” Max laughs. “I’m rather excited as I don’t know what to
expect, but let’s start the countdown.” Sant sits on the bottle rocket.
Sant grasps hold of the bottle as it darts into the sky. The class cheer for Sant.
They all stand in wonder thinking how far it will reach.
Sant closes his eyes to pretend his rocket has blasted all the way to the stars.
He imagines setting a path to Mars to become the first ant to step onto the red
planet. In reality, Sant has just passed over the top of the boys’ heads.
“What causes the bottle to launch, Mr Arthur?” asks Paul. “It all starts with the fizzy
tablet which fills the bottle with gas. The gas escapes and the lid pops open.
Water is pushed down and out of the bottle, causing it to blast off,” Mr Arthur
explains.
The class welcomes Sant back as he lands on the table. “You are the master at
riding the bottle rocket, Sant,” Mr Arthur smiles. “Next time, we can partner up and
test to see whose rocket goes the furthest.”

title: A kite contest
story:
The local school is holding a kite flying contest. Sant is showing the children how to
make the best kite. “You want to make your kite strong and light so it can fly high,”
Sant explains. “You will need string, sticks, tape, and bright paper.”
Mr Tom wants his class to watch a clip about the best kite flying tips. “What tips do
you have for us, Buzz?” asks Jazz. “Hold your kite by the top of the frame and let
the line out.” Buzz can’t wait to see the kites fly.
Jazz draws a wasp on her kite because she knows they are strong flyers. Cooper
chooses a swan as his kite mascot. “Swans glide across the water with grace.
I want my kite to fly across the sky with grace,” Cooper shares with the group.
Sant and Buzz offer to help find the winners of the kite contest. “I will watch for
kites that crash down. They are out of the contest,” says Sant. “I will fly up to see
which kite flies the highest.” Buzz starts to fly.
The day was perfect for kite flying. “Don’t stop running! We want the kites to lift on
the wind,” Sant calls as he watches from the stand. “Let go of the kite, Tim.
I think it will fly,” Cooper shouts. He is running fast.
“Our wasp kite is strong and flies so well!” Jazz is happy that their kite is up.
“How high do you think it will fly, Jazz?” Tina is watching Cooper and Tim’s kite fly
close to theirs. “I don’t know. Buzz is keeping watch to see which kite will be the
winner,” Jazz says.
“I hope the wasp team doesn’t win for flying the highest,” Cooper says as he holds
the line up high. “I hope our kite stays up and doesn’t crash,” Tim says with a
worried look. “I don’t think it will crash. After all, it is a swan kite and swans fly with
grace,” Cooper smiles.
“Well done, class! The wasp team’s kite was flying strong against the wind.
The swan team’s kite was gliding across the sky. Both kites flew high and didn’t
crash in the contest,” says Mr Tom happily. “Who wants to celebrate with
ice-cream?” “Me!” the children chime.

title: Riverside versus Dingoes
story:
It was the day of the big game. Ben was captain for the Riverside team. He held his
clipboard and counted all the players before they piled into the bus. It was going
to be a long bus ride to the footy ground.
When they arrived, the players began warming up. Dave and Henry jogged, while
others chose to practice passing and marking. Riverside were playing the Dingoes
for the second time in the season.
The last time the Dingoes played Riverside, the Dingoes were third on the ladder.
“Time to beat you,” Ben egged Gavin on. “I don’t think so,” Gavin called back.
The umpire, Spotty, blew his whistle to start the game.
The players ran into the middle of the ground. “I’ve got this,” called Gavin. “Run the
ball down to the goals, Riverside!” Coach Dan yelled. The Dingoes chased close
behind Riverside as they ran down the footy field.
Coach Dan added advice from the sideline, “Dave is free! Pass to Dave! Keep on
defending your players.” Riverside were up by one goal. Both teams had scored
well the entire game. There wasn’t a lot of time left on the clock.
Suddenly, the final whistle blew to signal the end of the match. Dave kicked one
more goal for Riverside. The Dingoes had lost but had good team spirit to say
‘well done’ to Riverside.
The team played hard and felt tired. Coach Dan was proud of them all.
“The Dingoes put in a good effort and tried to beat us. You used the ball well
across the ground and quickly moved it to our goals,” Coach Dan shared his
thinking on the game.
The team jumped into the bus and chatted about the game. They began to
unwind and felt satisfied that they tried their best and won. It was a great ride
home on the bus.

title: Missing biscuits
story:
Late in the day, Jim arrives home from school and heads to the kitchen for a snack.
“Mum, can I have a biscuit?” calls Jim. “First, I’d like you to put your lunchbox in the
sink,” says Mum.
Jim puts his lunchbox in the sink and reaches into the biscuit jar. He can’t wait to sit
down with a biscuit and relax after his long day at school. When Jim opens the jar,
he finds that all the biscuits are missing. His grin turns down into a frown.
“Mum! The biscuits are missing!” Mum quickly enters the kitchen. “I just filled the jar
today. This is a mystery!” “I wonder where they have vanished. I will solve this case
of the missing biscuits!” announces Jim.
Jim puts on his sleuth costume and begins to look for clues. He spots a trail of
biscuit crumbs leading from the jar to the back door. “I think I’m onto something,
Mum.” Jim runs outside. “I will find the guilty thief,” exclaims Jim.
Jim stands in his yard and finds a strange sight. Not only are there biscuit crumbs
trailing on the ground, but also evidence of chips. He looks towards his play gym,
and it has flowers all over it. “What is going on?” Jim wonders. He carefully walks
down to his play gym.
Jim finds Sant, Spotty, Buzz and Doug. Biscuits, chips, fizzy drink, and honey treats
are laid out ready to eat. “What is all this?” asks Jim. “We know how tired you are
after school, and we wanted to share a picnic with you,” Sant beams. “That is so
nice of you,” says Jim.
“It was a team effort.” Sant explains, “Spotty knows how to relax and strung up a
hammock on the play gym for you to rest. Buzz loves sweet treats and put food out
for us to share. Ants are good at carrying and moving things, so Doug and I found
flowers and hung them from the play gym.”
“Mystery solved!” Jim chuckles. Jim’s mum walks down to check on the afternoon
tea. “How is the picnic going?” she asks. “Great!” Jim smiles, “Typical of this crew
to be behind a tricky surprise like this.” They all giggle and enjoy their picnic in the
sun.

Grace and her family are going on a trip to see some interesting sites in a
city in the Pacific Northwest. The city is filled with exciting things to do and see.
There is a sentence on the travel website that describes it as a “must-see” spot!
Grace’s job was to plan their trip. She had a long list of what the family could do.
Grace said, “In the morning, we can go ice skating on the frozen lake. It faces
an iceberg. We could also walk to see the circle maze. There is a cedar totem
pole in the center.
“After lunch, we can race dog sleds! If we do that, we have to call and reserve
our spots. Only eight people can ride the sleds at one time,” Grace added.
“In the evening, we have to decide if we want to go to the dance or the palace
made of ice, ” she said. “We could also ice skate again,” Grace said with a smirk
on her face.
Her family was thrilled. She had picked something for everyone in the family.
That was a hard job.

much. Everything else is just perfect. Thank you, Grace!”

title: Caleb’s Cookbook
story:
For his birthday, Caleb asked for a new cookbook. He loved to fix meals with his
dad. They had been trying new dishes from different parts of the world.
His parents got him a cookbook from Italy. Caleb studied the cover. Under the
title, there was a picture of an open oven with big flames! Caleb was alarmed.
They did not have an oven like that! He asked his dad about this.
His dad laughed and explained, “Long ago, people in Italy used to cook bread in
wood-fired ovens. Today, many restaurants cook bread in brick ovens with a fire.
These are called wood-fired or brick ovens. And what do you think they cook the
most in them? Pizza!”
“That is so good,” said Caleb.
They first tried making plain flatbread, also known as pita. They measured flour,
milk, salt, and yogurt into a bowl.
Caleb and his dad stirred and kneaded the mixture. They rolled it into little balls
and flattened each ball with their hands. Dad explained that if they had a
wood-fired oven, they would slide the pieces of flatbread into the oven on a
wooden tray with a long handle. Instead, they placed them on a cookie sheet and
put them in their oven with a window in the door.
Caleb stood and watched through the window, and was surprised to see the
bread puff up while it cooked. It formed a pocket of air inside! When it was nice
and brown, Caleb gave Mom the first bite.
“Oh my goodness! This is wonderful,” she said.
Both Caleb and Dad had huge smiles on their faces. Caleb was surprised how
much he liked pita. “We should make pizza now, Dad!”

title: Chaos at the Castle Game
story:
There is a cool new game called “Chaos at the Castle.” I saw a sign that said it
was half price, so I asked my mom if I could get it! She is a school teacher, so of
course she gave me an assignment to write down why I think I need it. She said
she would give me an answer in a day or two.
Here are some of my reasons:
Every level has obstacles that I have to solve problems to overcome. One
example is I will have to figure out how to get past the gnomes that guard
the island and the castle.
You can only choose three tools to have with you. I will have to make smart
decisions about what I will most likely need. Some of the tools to choose
from are wrenches, swords, knives, and scissors
There are levels that require logic! One example is that there is a buffet full
of food like salmon, spaghetti, lamb chops, and raspberry pie. I will have to
use clues to solve the mystery of which food is making people sick.
The queen is in debt. I will look at all of her receipts and use my knowledge
of math to help her save money.
Other challenges require plumbing skills, removing a bomb, determining who
is being honest, wrestling with ghosts, and other cool things.
Look how much I will be using my brain! I doubt my mom can say no. What do
you think?

title: Checking on the Surf
story:
The girl burst into the kitchen. Her dad was washing the dishes. It was still
dark. The sun was just starting to come up.
Marla said, “I think the surf is big. Can we get into the car and go check
the swell? I can surf if it is not too strong.”
Dad said, “Marla, I still have so much to do. The porch is covered in dirt
from the storm.”
Marla turned on the charm. “Dad, if you let me go now, when I get back I
will do the porch, finish washing the dishes, and serve lunch! But the
perfect surf does not come very often, and it can get smaller fast. We
need to rush!”
Dad said, “Get your stuff. We can go check on it. But, if it is too big, you
cannot surf. I do not want you to get hurt.”
Marla turned with a twirl and said, “Yes! Thank you, Dad.”
They rushed to the cliffs to check the surf. It was not too big! The swell
was perfect.
Marla got her stuff and sprinted down the curved path to the surf. She
was one happy girl!

grass, sticks, and mud,” said Stan.

title: Dinner by the Fire
story:
One cold Friday night, Ty and Winnie got dropped off at home after
soccer practice. It was past dinner time, and they were hungry.
When they walked into the kitchen, there was nothing on the stove for
dinner. Also, they could not find their parents. They looked everywhere.
The kids wondered where their parents might be.
Then they heard their mom calling them: “Ty! Winnie! Come to the
backyard! Put your coat and hat on!”
This was very strange. They couldn’t think of why they wanted them in the
backyard. It was dark, cold, and time to eat!
Winnie said, “What is going on?”
Ty said, “I don’t know. Have they been hiding something from us?”
They went into the backyard. The light from the moon and stars shone
brightly from high in the sky. As they turned the corner, they saw
flickering blazes of fire. Ty and Winnie grinned with delight. Their parents
had made a huge bonfire!
Dad said, “We decided to do something different tonight. It is too cold
to go camping, but we’re going to have a family hot dog roast right
here in our backyard. Grab a chair. Get one of the roasting forks.
It’s dinner time!”
They all roasted hotdogs on long forks that had white rubber handles.
The hotdogs were so tasty that they each had two!
After dinner, the children wanted dessert. There was a warm s’mores
pie with ice cream. They had a bowl full. The bonfire dinner was a
fantastic surprise!

title: Duke
story:
Duke is a super cute dog! He has curly black fur, a wide white stripe on his back,
and white spots on his chest. Duke lives with Wade, who is his best buddy.
Duke is huge, but he thinks he is a baby. He likes to cuddle all the time and for
people to rub his belly. He is full of energy, too! He likes to chase rabbits and
play pull-the-rope with Wade. He is also very smart. He can respond to
commands like shake, sit, come, and roll over. He is such a cute animal.
Wade includes Duke in everything he does. When Wade gets in his truck, Duke rides, too.
Wade has a pet store. Duke goes to work with him. The store is an animal
kingdom! The shelves are fully stocked. They have kibble, stuffed animals, pet
beds, bones, and more. He even has costumes for animals!
One time Wade put a costume on Duke. The workers at the store were amused.
Duke was dressed up like a rubber ducky. He didn’t quack, but he did bark. It
was funny!
Duke has some quirks. One quirk of his is that he does not like strong smells,
such as perfume. He barks when he smells perfume! He is also funny about the
volume level. He will whine if it is too much for him.
Duke makes everyone smile. He is so unique and has the best attitude. There
isn’t another dog like him.

the day she was having the party she always wanted! Fay’s dad and grandma made a
list of things to do on a page in her writing tablet.
Fay’s Party
Invite friends.
Plan the games.
Play pin the Tail on the Mermaid.
•
Make bracelets and necklaces.
•
Face paint
•
Things to eat
cupcakes
•

up the grill in the rain! Her grandma braided her hair into a fishtail. All of her friends

Ms. Greta is our first grade teacher. She got us a gerbil to be our class pet.
We named her Ginger. Ms. Greta says she loves gerbils as much as she loves
gems. We must take good care of Ginger!
Ms. Greta has a huge chart above Ginger’s cage. It has a list of tips to
help us take care of Ginger. This is what the chart says:
Be gentle with Ginger.
You are a giant compared to Ginger. Sit while you play with her.
Wash your hands before and after you hold Ginger. We do not want
to share our germs.
Clean the gym in Ginger’s cage.
Feed Ginger the food from the gold box.
One day a week, we will feed Ginger cabbage. She thinks it is so good!
Be sure to close the gate to Ginger’s cage!
If Ginger is acting strange, tell Ms. Greta!
After spending time with Ginger, we all love her as much as gems, too!

title: Hike, Bike, Swim
story:
Mike and Cate are doing a triathlon. In this triathlon, they will hike up a
hill for six miles, bike on a path for twenty-five miles, and swim across a
lake for one mile. They begin the event at six o’clock.
It starts with the hike. It is the hardest because it is uphill. There are many
stones and sharp branches that can poke them, so they watch for those
as they walk. When they get to the summit, they are tired. They take a sip
of the lime drink they packed to quench their thirst.
After a little while, they get their helmets on, strike the pedals on their
bike, and take off! They ride down the hill and over to the lake. They have
a map in case they get lost. The map has a white, curvy line on it to show
them the path.
At the lake, they jump in. Mike and Cate are hot. They are glad to get in
the water, but one mile is far to swim! They were not fast, but they
finished.
They are brimming with pride at the finish line. What a life!

story:
Kevin was so happy. He rented a van to go on a trip with his son, Max.
They were off to see the Top Shock Falls!
The falls were up in the hills. The path was very muddy and slick. The van
skidded, but Kevin kept it on track. When they got there, they watched the
falls from the van. The falls crashed and thudded onto the jagged rocks.
Max wanted to get next to the falls.
Kevin said, “We can go, but get your jacket. You will want to have it.”
It was damp when they exited the van. They went up the rocks to get next
to the Top Shock Falls. Standing next to them, they got misted a lot. The
current going into the falls was very fast. Sometimes it splashed hard on
the rocks. When it did, Kevin and Max got drenched!
Max and his dad were very glad that they visited the falls. They crossed it
off the list of things they wanted to see.

find something cute to wear.”

the trick! Happy hunting.”
The Vintage Closet is a thrift store on Main Street. Pru loved shopping at
thrift stores because the clothes were valued at a fair price. They also had
one-of-a-kind things!
Today, Pru was hoping to find some new jeans for the dance. Luckily, they
had a large supply of jeans in every hue. Pru wanted to find black skinny

Cute! Cute! Cute!
Pru went to pay. She had just enough money to buy the jeans. She smiled
knowing that she got a bargain for her jeans and that they were perfect
to wear to the dance.

and Jake to do. She gives them the same wage, but they have different
jobs. The note this morning said,
Jobs for Jake:
Rake the yard.
Take the dishes from your room to the sink.
Make your bed.
Pick up your games.
Jobs for Rose:
Make your bed.
Carry the trash to the bin.
Take the chicken dish that is on the stove to the lady that lives

Fix lunch for you and Jake.

was done, she left it on the table. When she came back to the kitchen, she
saw that Jake ate the whole plate of cake! He was in a bad state. His

The farm has a big red barn at the edge of the yard. Our family of six
lives there with many pets. We have a dog, two cats, seven pigs, and a
flock of ducks.
There is a lot for us to do! We start at six.
Carla has to watch the flock and give them pellets for lunch.
Mark has to wash the pigs. The pigs dig far into the mud. Yuck! They
are such a mess!
Art has to cut the fallen branches into small chunks. He has a big saw
to help with this job.
Mom spins yarn into hats and scarves.
The dog thinks his job is to be the family’s alarm. When anyone comes
into the yard, he barks a warning.
The cats catch any rats that are in the barn.
Dad fills up the car with items and goes to the farmers market. He
sells eggs, ham, hats, and scarves.
Living on the farm can be hard, but we all do our part.

title: Planning a Trip
story:
Eve and Pete have been stuck at home for quite some time. They long to
be able to take plane rides or even mere drives in the car to see and do
fun things. They often say to their mom, “I want to be anywhere but here!”
While they have been at home, they have spent a lot of time on their
laptops. There are travel websites that have photos of the best spots to
visit. On these sites, they find out so much from skimming the comments
and the answers people give others. Eve and Pete take notes so they do
not forget anything.
Eve wishes to go to spots that are by the water. She wants to watch
sunsets from the white sand shores of Mexico. She wants to hike around
Crater Lake. The water looks so pretty there.
Pete has hopes to go see the Grand Canyon and some huge waterfalls. He
saw some sand dunes that people surf on, and it looked like fun. That is at
the top of his list!
When they are able, Eve and Pete will travel, and they have lots of spots
to pick from for their next trip.

title: Ports and Harbors
story:
Ports and harbors are both spots on the water where ships and vessels
go to dock, but they are different.
Ports are for ships that transport cargo and travelers. At ports that
transport cargo, men and women are often busy doing hard labor. It is
common to see them running forklifts. The forklifts help transfer big
boxes from the ship. They stack those boxes in an orderly manner on the
dock.
At ports that transport travelers, there are big ships and small ships for
travelers. The travelers are often going on trips that you cannot get to
by land.
At a harbor, you will see both big and small vessels. Men and women
often park there to get off and have some fun. Some also park the
vessels there to protect them in the winter. On some docks in a harbor,
you can see kids fishing or fishermen unpacking the catch from the day.
Both ports and harbors are important to folks who do work or have fun
on the water.

title: Rowdy on Broadway
story:
Rowdy is an actor. Actors do more than just perform. They have to learn
the script and study the topic to understand the outlook of the character
they will play. Rowdy was cast as the lead in a Broadway show about the
challenges of a rancher. This role was very different from his real life.
Rowdy had a lot to learn about life on a ranch.
In the play, the rancher discovers some bad news. His prized brown cow
fell down and was found hurt in the field.
The hurt cow is a big problem for the rancher because the yearly roundup
is only a few weeks away. A roundup is an event where livestock is
brought together to be bought and sold. An injured animal has a lower
value than a healthy animal, so it will sell for less money.
In his role as the rancher, Rowdy will need to act completely stressed out!
He has to figure out a way to get that prized cow feeling better! Most of
the play is about the silly ways the rancher tried to help the cow.
By the end of the play, though, the rancher found a way to help the cow
recover. They travel to the crowded roundup, and he sells the brown cow
for a good amount.
Rowdy learned so much from his role in the play. He now knew more
about the difference between country life and city life. It is almost like
being on two separate planets!

Bertha and her sister, Nora, have been running partners for as long as
they both can remember. They run together every morning. They try to
never miss a day.
One day after their run, the girls were hungry and very thirsty. Bertha
and Nora had a number of spots over by the river that they went to
often for lunch. The Fresh Farmer is the one next to the park and is a bit
further, but it is the best.
The menu has yogurt, tarts, salads, sandwiches, and burgers. Everything
they have is superb. Bertha ordered first. She got a salad to help give
her some energy. Nora ordered a sandwich to help fill her up. They both
felt so much better afterwards.
They went over to sit on soft, pretty chairs on the deck. The girls
watched furry squirrels run under the deck. They were glad they were
not the ones running.

title: Running and Watching
story:
It is sunny, so Jimmy is going for a run. While he is running, he is watching to
see what all the folks are doing to have fun.
Jimmy sees a daddy sitting on a bench rocking his baby. The dad is humming a
song.
On a patch of sod, a kid is catching softballs with his mom.
Jimmy runs by a pond and there is a dog swimming. A man is yelling to him,
“Come back, Buddy!” Jimmy thinks the man is mad at his dog.
At the end of the pond, a duck is hidden in the brush. Jimmy cannot see it, but it
is quacking so much. He thinks the duck may be stuck, so he goes to help. The
duck is not stuck. He is just splashing in the muck.
On the way back, he sees a bunny hopping along a hedge of shrubs.
Two gals are sitting on a blanket in the sun. One of them is being silly and one is
grinning so big!
When Jimmy was done with his run, he was so glad for getting out in the sun.

title: Seeking Nuts for Winter
story:
hear feet tree leave please between really move
Every fall the squirrels begin their work to prepare for winter. This means
that they are really busy gathering nuts. The squirrels scamper and chirp
as they run quickly from place to place.
Most squirrels hunt for nuts in at least three different places. They seek
them hanging from green tree branches, in the leaves, and near the
trunks. Squirrels can leap many feet which helps them move from tree to
tree.
The squirrels get nuts and hold them briefly inside both of their cheeks.
Then they move them to their nest. Squirrels keep the same storage spots
for years. The animals use old hollow parts of tree trunks as a hiding
place. Sometimes they will even steal from another squirrel – a squirrel thief!
If the squirrels have nuts to eat, they can go for a week between each
meal. This yield is key when it is freezing. They can sleep when it is too cold
to be awake and do not have to find things to eat. What a relief!
If you happen to locate a stash of nuts, please leave it alone. Don’t take
them! A squirrel depends on the nuts for survival.

title: Stormy the Horse
story:
This is Thorn’s story of the morning Stormy was born.
“The horse was going to be born in the grassy yard, but we had to switch
plans. There was a bad storm, so the horse had to be birthed in a stall. The
walls of the barn were shuddering in the strong winds. The horse was
standing in her stall and she was not doing well. She was frantic.
I was thinking I needed some support to help this horse relax. All of a
sudden, Jamar and Ford ran into the barn. They had a carpet for her to
rest on. We quickly swept the stall and washed out the dirt. We put the
carpet in the corner of her stall. Her comfort was very important to us all.
Then we all gathered next to the horse and offered her support until the
baby was born.
That baby was strong! When he got here, he got up so fast. We call him
Stormy. He is our baby horse that was born in a storm.” Thorn grinned.

title: The Apple Puzzle
story:
There was a puzzle on the little desk in the kitchen. The example on the front
of the box was of a bunch of apples. Omar wanted to put it together, but it
was not going to be simple.
Uncle Marco was there visiting. He did puzzles a lot. He offered Omar a tip on
how to tackle the puzzle.
“Start from the edges and work to the middle,” Uncle Marco said.
Omar’s father gave him a snack to nibble on, and then he and Uncle Marco
left to go into the den to talk.
Omar got started. There were one hundred parts in the puzzle. Omar got the
parts that formed the edge of the puzzle first. He stuck them all together.
The hard part was going to be the middle. That was where all the apples were,
and there was a lot of red! Omar had to inspect the example on the box a lot.
It was a struggle. He turned, twisted, and wiggled parts until they all finally
fit together.
Omar did the puzzle all by himself. He was so happy!

She filled her shopping cart quickly with the stuff and went to the park.
The party was a hit. Martin sold thirty canvases and was asked to do
more. Lara told lots of folks about the garden and how to help with it.
It was a fun party!

story:
We went on a bus to a museum for a class trip.
They had an art exhibit where everything was made from cubes. One
artist made a life-sized animal of just cubes!
There was a play zone with a huge tube slide. We got to go down it. It
went very fast and had twenty curves. We landed in a big ball pit.
In the discovery zone, we saw a demo of how a fuse works. A fuse
protects the things that are plugged in at our home. It stops electricity
that is too hot by melting the line before it comes into our home. The
fumes from the melting line smelled so bad.
We also got to see pure stones. Miss Jules told us how pure stones were
different from other stones. We got to take a stone home with us.
The last zone was the animal zone. We got to touch a mule. It was so cute!
They told us that mules are a mix of a donkey and a horse. They are hard
workers and live a long time!
We almost missed our bus because we were having so much fun.

title: The Field Trip to the Zoo
story:
Summer break was almost here, and the school had planned an
end-of-year trip for the students. Hugo’s first grade class was on their
way to the zoo. The students were ecstatic!
It was a cool June morning at the zoo, and very few people had arrived,
yet. Soon the zoo would be full of visitors. The class entered through the
gates bursting with energy.
Lulu the monkey was in the trees with her troop. The zoo keeper had just
dropped off food. They had fresh fruit for breakfast. Lulu was chewing on
a mango. She was slinging mango juice everywhere!
In the garden, the plants were covered in dew, making them sparkle. The
plants had not been pruned back, so they were covered in colorful
blooms, too! Hugo’s favorite was the Lily of the Nile. Its petals were a
pretty bright blue.
A group of pink flamingos were standing in the pond. It was filled with
troupes of shrimp. The flamingos wade through the water to find their meal.
After the flamingos, the students wandered through the tiger’s den. They
saw the elephants bathing themselves with mud. They got to feed the
giraffes! It was interesting to learn about all of these animals.
Then it was time to go.
The kids groaned, “No. Not yet. Please can we stay longer?”
Their teacher said, “Sorry, crew. It’s time to load up on the bus.”
The class had a great time on their zoo field trip. They couldn’t wait to go back.

title: The Homesick Pilot
story:
Collins was homesick. She missed her entire family and felt alone when
she was gone for work. She was a pilot and liked to fly, but she did not like
the hotel life. She was most alive when she was at home with her husband
and their children.
Collins sat inside the cockpit. The plane was flying north to the state of
Montana, where she lived. The expected time for the plane to arrive in
Bozeman was just after sunrise. They would land on time! She liked it
when she could see the alpine forests. She was close to home then!
The plane landed. Collins completed her checklist and grabbed her bags.
Despite being tired from nine days of travel combined with the six-hour
trip she just made, she still dashed from the plane and down the terminal.
She was polite as she stepped aside for people and zigzagged toward the exit.
The plan was that, if she was quick, she could get home before the
children got on the bus.
What she did not know was that her family had come to surprise her.
When Collins stepped outside to catch a ride share, she saw her whole
little family standing on the curb. Her children ran and gave her a long
hug. “We missed you, Mommy!” they yelled with excitement.
Thank goodness she was back on land and with her favorite people.

watched until her shiny red auto turned off their street.
Every day, Saul would feel sad when his mom left. He liked when they
were all home together.
Dad knew how awful Saul felt about his mom leaving. He tried to distract
him with fun things to do.
“Do you want to draw something?” Dad asked.

“Would you like to play on the seesaw?” Dad asked.
“No, not really,” said Saul.
“Why don’t we do a jigsaw puzzle?” said Dad.
Saul smiled. He liked puzzles. “Yes! Let’s do a puzzle.”
Saul and Dad worked on the puzzle together. He forgot he was upset and
had fun with his father.

title: The Math Problem
story:
+ =
Dane was doing his math homework at the table while he ate some
grapes. He hates math, and word problems are very hard for him. He was
frustrated because he had all these mistakes, but he did not know why.
Dane yelled, “This is so hard. I want to quit and escape to somewhere that
has no math problems.”
His sister Katelin likes math. She came to help.
“Dane,” she said. “You are irate, and it is not helping. Inhale for three
seconds, and then exhale for three seconds. You need to get rid of all this
anger. You can solve this problem. You are smart!”
Dane did it. He could feel his body deflate.
“Now, erase your answer, and let’s do it together,” Katelin said.
The problem says, “The bakery had eight pancakes and four cupcakes in
the case. How many items are in the case?”
“We can use these grapes to help you answer the problem,” Katelin said. “Get
eight grapes from your plate for the number of pancakes in the case. Now, get four
more grapes for the number of cupcakes. How many total grapes do you have?”
Dane said, “Twelve.”
“That’s correct! You will be amazed at how well you can do math if you use
objects to help translate what the problem is asking,” said Katelin.
Dane smiled and embraced her.

title: The Pen Pal Project
story:
When I was in the third grade, Miss Smith gave me and the other kids in my
class a small, square-shaped box. Inside, there was the name of a person, a
note, nine white cards to write letters on, and a roll of tape.
Miss Smith told us that our new pen pal was the person whose name was in
our box. They were from another state. We could not trade pen pals with our
friends. The one that came in the box was the one we would get to know.
She gave us some rules.
You should not give your home address to your pen pal. That is not safe.
You cannot send any photos of people.
You can tape photos of spots you like to visit or art if you would like.
You have to use the rules of English as you write your letters. This will
help you develop your craft.
Miss Smith let us skim our notes and share things our pen pal wrote.
One student wrote about the skate ramps in the park. Another told a story
about how he had to slide into home base to win the big game. My pen pal,
Etta, rode her bike across two states.
I have never forgotten this project. Etta and I are still pen pals today.

title: The Stampede
story:
It was an extremely hot evening. Jolene is an athlete, and her game
ended late. She was driving home hot and tired. She just wanted to go to
bed. All of a sudden, she had to stop. There were buffalo everywhere!
A stampede thundered on the pavement around her small car. The herd
was in a frantic run. Her little vehicle rattled and jiggled along with the
concrete under her. She felt like the size of a centipede compared to the
size of these massive buffalo!
The animals rushed by. Something must have startled them and made
them run. She could only see a sphere-shaped object to her left, but she
could not see what it was. It was so dark!
Jolene was a little scared. The buffalo merely had to brush the side and
the car would rock. They could crush her car! She had a string of things
going through her mind: “Am I safe here in my car? Should I try to drive?
I can’t think of who I can call to help! I don’t understand what is going on!”
Moments later, the dust began to settle. The last of the buffalo passed by
her. She had never felt like this in all of her life. How and why did that
happen? She would have this scene stuck in her mind forever. Jolene
would never forget the stampede.

title: Watching the Buffalo and Elk
story:
At dusk one evening, my family went to a vast grassy spot to watch the
animals that go there for dinner. The sun was just beginning to set. This
was the perfect moment to see the animals.
The buffalo were walking in the grass. They had shaggy thick fur, big
chests, short legs, and tall horns. They stopped often to get big clumps of
grass and to drink water from the river.
My mother whispered to my brothers and me, “Be silent. The animals are
shy. They will relax if we are quiet. They will not run from us if we respect
them.”
Just then, another herd of animals came to the river. What luck! They had
thick fur, tall antlers, but long legs. The herd of elk were just as pretty as
photos I saw on my computer.
My family sat silently and watched the herds until it was dark. Then the
buffalo and elk walked beside the river, far beyond the trees and brush, to
find a spot to nap.

title: Watching the Frog

“Why is he ribbiting?” asked Chad.

“What is he telling us?” asked Chad.
“A ribbit can tell lots of things, but I think the frog is telling us that this is
his spot,” said Elly.
They watched him as he hopped onto the lily pad. Plop! Then the frog
jumped into the pond and went swimming.
“I didn’t think frogs swam. How is he doing that?” asked Chad.
“Frogs have strong back legs,” Elly said. “His strong back legs and
webbed feet help propel him in the pond,” said Elly.
They watched as the frog swam. He was going to the flat rocks. He was
not fast. The frog inched himself to the edge. When he got to the rocks, he
popped up.
Now the frog is sitting still and basking in the sun.

title: Youth Troop Soup!
story:
Silas was excited about forming a cooking club in his neighborhood. This
new youth group would meet in his mom’s kitchen at ten o’clock on
Saturdays. Silas expected two other boys, plus a few girls who would be
in the troop. Silas asked his mom if they could make some soup. Mom
took a cookbook from the shelf that was all about soup!
“Should we let the group pick which soup to cook?” Silas asked his mom.
“Well,” said his mom, “Let’s pick the first one, since we will need to make
sure we have on-hand what we need.”
“Then I say we make split pea soup!” Silas yelled.
“Split pea soup should be nice and thick and more like a stew,” said Mom.
“In fact, the key to this soup is to make it so thick that you can stand a
wooden spoon in it!”
Silas and Mom headed for the store. Silas took notes while Mom listed a
few items they would choose: three onions, a bag of carrots, a jar of beef
bouillon cubes, and one bag of dried green peas. “We will use salt and
pepper,” Mom said, “but we have some in the pantry nook.”
When Silas’s friends arrived on Saturday, they gathered in the kitchen and
stood around the table. His mom had made a task list for each friend. The
troop got going! Mom reminded them that it would take awhile for the
peas to get soft to make the thick soup.
When it was done, they tried to stand the spoon in their soup. It was thick,
but not thick enough. They let it simmer a little longer. Then they used a
ladle to scoop the soup into bowls for each friend. Silas had the first taste.
“Oh my goodness! This is wonderful,” he said. “Let’s look at the cookbook
and choose what we will cook next Saturday, troop!”
